title: Cancer: current or history, and metastases
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's cancer as documented at this visit.
note:
Chief Complaint: Follow-up for metastatic disease.

HPI: Copied Forward: Patient is a 78-year-old woman with a history of cancer of the right breast. The primary malignancy was surgically removed and treated several years ago. Follow-up imaging has historically shown no evidence of local recurrence at the primary site. Treatment for the primary site is complete.
Update: Patient presents today for evaluation of systemic progression. She reports new onset of fatigue and mild abdominal discomfort. She notes that she has been stable otherwise since her last imaging.

Medication List: 
- Lisinopril 10mg daily
- Atorvastatin 20mg daily

Vitals: BP 128/82, HR 74, SpO2 98% on room air, Temp 98.6F.

Review of Systems:
- Constitutional: Positive for fatigue.
- Gastrointestinal: Positive for mild abdominal discomfort.
- Musculoskeletal: Negative.
- Neurological: Negative.
- Cardiovascular: Negative.

Exam:
General: Well-appearing, alert and oriented x3.
Abdomen: Soft, non-tender, no guarding.
Skin: No new lesions noted.

Assessment:
1. Liver metastases: New imaging confirms progression of the malignant neoplasm to the liver.
2. History of cancer of the right breast: Stable with no evidence of local recurrence at the original site.

Plan:
1. Discussed liver metastases with the patient.
2. Order CT abdomen/pelvis to monitor progression.
3. Referral to oncology for systemic management of the liver involvement.

Electronically signed, 
R. Mensah, NP
05/14/2026
explanations: The right female breast cancer was excised or eradicated, no treatment is directed to it and there is no evidence of it: personal history Z85.3 (no HCC). Any metastasis is still coded as a current secondary malignancy.
Liver metastases: C78.7, secondary malignant neoplasm of liver (HCC 17).

distractors.why: Treatment ended and there is no evidence of the primary: code personal history (Z85), not active cancer.
Metastasis is coded as a secondary malignancy, even when the primary is history.
The metastases are in the liver, not bone.

hccs.label: Cancer Metastatic to Lung/Liver/Brain/and Other Organs; Acute Myeloid Leukemia Except Promyelocytic
